<a id="rome_steps_ratings"></a>
**`rome_steps_ratings`**

**The same checks, applied the other way: Rome's steps are disputed under every
standard.** Westminster's answer to Trent's premise about merit, and the
Reformed reconciliation's answers to canon 24's step and chapter 16's, each
argue from texts and rest on no one's word alone. So each counts as an argument
under the evidence standard as under the tradition standard, and each of Trent's
claims is `disputed` under both.

Set beside `fruit_step_ratings`, this is the difference the checks find. The
Reformed objections to Trent's claims are arguments under each of the three
standards. Trent's objections to the Reformed step are arguments only under the
standard that allows the council's word.

What this does not claim: that either side's step is right.

```lean
theorem rome_steps_ratings : meritPremise.ratings = [(Standard.evidence,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6"]), (Standard.tradition,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6"]), (Standard.scriptural,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6"])] ∧ canon24Step.ratings =
    [(Standard.evidence, Computed.disputedBy ["The Reformed harmony
    (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"]), (Standard.tradition, Computed.disputedBy
    ["The Reformed harmony (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"]),
    (Standard.scriptural, Computed.disputedBy ["The Reformed harmony
    (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"])] ∧ rewardStep.ratings = [(Standard.evidence,
    Computed.disputedBy ["The Reformed harmony (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"]),
    (Standard.tradition, Computed.disputedBy ["The Reformed harmony
    (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"]), (Standard.scriptural, Computed.disputedBy
    ["The Reformed harmony (Westminster XVI.2, XVI.5)"])]
-- axioms: propext
```

<a id="westminster_answers_from_the_texts"></a>
**`westminster_answers_from_the_texts`**

**Westminster's answer rests on no one's word alone; Trent's claim does.** Every
claim that Westminster's reading of the reward states outright is a text it
gives as a proof. The one claim chapter 16 adds to its texts, that the reward is
given to merits, is the council's own.

```lean
theorem westminster_answers_from_the_texts :
    westminsterOnReward.restingOnAuthority = [] ∧
    trentOnReward.restingOnAuthority = [Claim.rewardRenderedToMerits]
-- axioms: propext
```

#### Trent's definition, and whether faith suffices

<a id="trentSufficiencySource"></a>
**`trentSufficiencySource`**

Trent's step from its definition to the denial that faith suffices. If
justification is the renewal of the inward person by charity poured in, then
faith, "unless hope and charity be added thereto, neither unites man perfectly
with Christ" (Session VI, ch. 7), and whoever says that "nothing else is
required to co-operate" is anathema (canon 9). Rated `disputed`: the Reformed
read Luke 18 and Luke 7:50 as a plea that sufficed (`luke18Line`).

```lean
def trentSufficiencySource : Source :=
  {
    primary :=
      Reference.work tannerDecrees
        (Bib.Locus.sectionRef
          "Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, ch. 7; canon 9"),
    tradition := Tradition.romanCatholic, confidence := Confidence.disputed }
```

<a id="trentSufficiencyLine"></a>
**`trentSufficiencyLine`** — Faith does not suffice (Trent, ch. 7, canon 9)

**Faith does not suffice, from Trent's definition** (ch. 7, canon 9): the
definition, and the step from it. This states Trent's denial as these pages
state it throughout, as a consequence of what Trent says justification is
(`trentDefinitionSteps`).

<div class="testimony-math">

\begin{aligned}

\text{(2)} \quad &amp; \href{#claim-33}{P_{33}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{#claim-26}{P_{26}} \\[4pt]

\]

<a id="romansFourOnWordAssessment"></a>
**`romansFourOnWordAssessment`**

**Romans 4, on Paul's word, against Trent's definition taken as a claim about
the word.** Paul explains the righteousness God counts to the ungodly as sin not
counted (4:5–8), and by the rule of least meaning his verb means no more than
that verdict. It argues from Paul's own text, without assuming the courtroom
sense. So it is an argument under all three standards, and the strongest known
against taking the definition this way.

**Dissent:** *Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word*, against *Trent: Paul's δικαιόω denotes renewal (ch. 8, with Augustine)*. ✔ A critique: it can be held with the step's grounds, and it argues its denial by a step of its own.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✔ yes | — |
| tradition | ✔ yes | — |
| Scripture | ✔ yes | — |

<a id="lexicalOnWordAssessment"></a>
**`lexicalOnWordAssessment`**

**The argument from Paul's word, against Trent's definition taken as a claim
about the word.** It holds as a premise that Paul's "justify" is a verdict and
*not* making righteous, and that premise, by what it means, already denies
Trent's reading (`Meanings.SolaFide.joins`). So against that reading it is a
rival reading held as a premise, and by the checks a disagreement, not an
argument. It rests on the lexicon, and it stands or falls with that premise's
own rating. Trent's reading stands in the same place against it
(`trentWordOnLexicalAssessment`).

**Dissent:** *Paul's word (by the rule of least meaning)*, against *Trent: Paul's δικαιόω denotes renewal (ch. 8, with Augustine)*. ✘ A disagreement, not a critique: what it asserts outright already contradicts the step's conclusion, so no step of its own argues it.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✘ no | — |
| tradition | ✘ no | — |
| Scripture | ✘ no | — |

<a id="luke18OnSufficiencyAssessment"></a>
**`luke18OnSufficiencyAssessment`**

**Luke 18, against Trent's step to "faith does not suffice".** The tax
collector's plea, without works, and God's verdict. It can be held together with
Trent's definition, the step's starting point, and argues that the plea
sufficed. An argument under all three standards.

**Dissent:** *Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)*, against *Faith does not suffice (Trent, ch. 7, canon 9)*. ✔ A critique: it can be held with the step's grounds, and it argues its denial by a step of its own.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✔ yes | — |
| tradition | ✔ yes | — |
| Scripture | ✔ yes | — |

<a id="definitionPremise"></a>
**`definitionPremise`**

**Trent's definition, with the objections to it**: Paul's gospel and Romans 4.

**The rating, computed.** *Trent: justification is the renewal of the inward man (ch. 7)* is cited at *disputed* ([Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, ch. 7; [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), canon 11). Dissents encoded: *Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1)*, *Romans 4:3–8*. The strongest known: *Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1)*.

| Standard | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | **disputed** | a credible critique: Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1); Romans 4:3–8 |
| tradition | **disputed** | a credible critique: Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1); Romans 4:3–8 |
| Scripture | **disputed** | a credible critique: Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1); Romans 4:3–8 |

<a id="wordPremise"></a>
**`wordPremise`**

**Trent's reading of Paul's word, with the objections to it**: Romans 4 on the
word, the strongest known, and the argument from Paul's word.

**The rating, computed.** *Trent: Paul's δικαιόω denotes renewal (ch. 8, with Augustine)* is cited at *disputed* ([Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, chs. 7–8; [VanLandingham 2006](../bibliography.md#vanlandingham-judgment-justification-2006)). Dissents encoded: *Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word*, *Paul's word (by the rule of least meaning)*. The strongest known: *Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word*.

| Standard | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | **disputed** | a credible critique: Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word |
| tradition | **disputed** | a credible critique: Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word |
| Scripture | **disputed** | a credible critique: Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word |

<a id="sufficiencyStep"></a>
**`sufficiencyStep`**

**Trent's step to "faith does not suffice", with the objection to it**: Luke 18.

**The rating, computed.** *Faith does not suffice (Trent, ch. 7, canon 9)* is cited at *disputed* ([Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, ch. 7; canon 9). Dissents encoded: *Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)*. The strongest known: *Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)*.

| Standard | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | **disputed** | a credible critique: Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified) |
| tradition | **disputed** | a credible critique: Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified) |
| Scripture | **disputed** | a credible critique: Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified) |

<a id="trent_definition_ratings"></a>
**`trent_definition_ratings`**

**Trent's definition, and what follows from it, are disputed under every
standard.** Taken as a claim about what God does, the definition is met by
Paul's gospel and Romans 4. Taken as a claim about Paul's word, it is met by
Romans 4's explanation of the verb. Its step to "faith does not suffice" is met
by Luke 18. Each of those argues from texts and from evidence anyone can check,
so each is an argument under each of the three standards.

What this does not claim: that the definition is false. `disputed` means there
is an argued objection, not that the objection wins.

```lean
theorem trent_definition_ratings : definitionPremise.ratings =
    [(Standard.evidence, Computed.disputedBy ["Paul's gospel (Galatians 1;
    Westminster XI.1)", "Romans 4:3–8"]), (Standard.tradition,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Paul's gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1)",
    "Romans 4:3–8"]), (Standard.scriptural, Computed.disputedBy ["Paul's
    gospel (Galatians 1; Westminster XI.1)", "Romans 4:3–8"])] ∧
    wordPremise.ratings = [(Standard.evidence, Computed.disputedBy ["Romans
    4:3–8, on Paul's word"]), (Standard.tradition, Computed.disputedBy
    ["Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word"]), (Standard.scriptural,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Romans 4:3–8, on Paul's word"])] ∧
    sufficiencyStep.ratings = [(Standard.evidence, Computed.disputedBy ["Luke
    18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)"]), (Standard.tradition,
    Computed.disputedBy ["Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)"]),
    (Standard.scriptural, Computed.disputedBy ["Luke 18:9–14 (the tax
    collector justified)"])]
-- axioms: propext
```

<a id="trentWordOnLexicalAssessment"></a>
**`trentWordOnLexicalAssessment`**

**Trent's reading of Paul's word, against the step about the word.** It argues
its conclusion from Augustine's explanation. But what it concludes, that Paul's
"justify" means making righteous, is what the step's first starting point
denies: that starting point says the verb is a verdict *and not* making
righteous (`Meanings.SolaFide.joins`). So it objects to that starting point and
not to the step, and belongs to the rating of the starting point, under any
standard.

**Dissent:** *Trent, with Augustine (ch. 8)*, against *Paul's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*. ✘ A dissent from the step's grounds, not from the step: it denies one of them.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✘ no | — |
| tradition | ✘ no | — |
| Scripture | ✘ no | — |

<a id="trentGraceOnGospelAssessment"></a>
**`trentGraceOnGospelAssessment`**

**Trent's definition taken as a claim about what God does, against the step in
Paul's gospel.** It holds the definition as a premise, and that premise alone
contradicts the step's conclusion. A disagreement, not an argument, under each
of the three standards.

**Dissent:** *Trent, read as what God does (ch. 7; Joint Declaration §22)*, against *Paul's gospel: a verdict on a finished work is no renewal*. ✘ A disagreement, not a critique: what it asserts outright already contradicts the step's conclusion, so no step of its own argues it.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✘ no | Justification is not remission of sins only, but renewal of the inward man; The inward renewal of the justified grows as they do good works in grace |
| tradition | ✘ no | — |
| Scripture | ✘ no | Justification is not remission of sins only, but renewal of the inward man; The inward renewal of the justified grows as they do good works in grace |

<a id="trentSufficiencyOnLuke18Assessment"></a>
**`trentSufficiencyOnLuke18Assessment`**

**Trent's denial that faith suffices, against Luke 18's step.** It is argued,
from its definition, and it accepts the parable. Its one starting point is the
definition, which rests on the council's word. So it is an argument under the
tradition standard only.

**Dissent:** *Trent, ch. 7 and canon 9*, against *Luke 18:9–14 (the tax collector justified)*. ✔ A critique: it can be held with the step's grounds, and it argues its denial by a step of its own.

| Standard | A credible critique? | Rests on what the standard does not accept |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | ✘ no | Justification is not remission of sins only, but renewal of the inward man |
| tradition | ✔ yes | — |
| Scripture | ✘ no | Justification is not remission of sins only, but renewal of the inward man |

<a id="lexicalWordStep"></a>
**`lexicalWordStep`**

**The step about Paul's word, with the objection to it**: Trent's reading of the
word, the strongest known.

**The rating, computed.** *Paul's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)* is cited at *well supported* ([Silva 1994](../bibliography.md#silva-biblical-words-1994); [Moo 1996](../bibliography.md#moo-romans-1996), §p. 80; [Barr 2004](../bibliography.md#barr-semantics-2004)). Dissents encoded: *Trent, with Augustine (ch. 8)*. The strongest known: *Trent, with Augustine (ch. 8)*.

| Standard | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| evidence | **well supported** | every encoded dissent fails a check, the strongest known among them, so the step's support stands |
| tradition | **well supported** | every encoded dissent fails a check, the strongest known among them, so the step's support stands |
| Scripture | **well supported** | every encoded dissent fails a check, the strongest known among them, so the step's support stands |

<a id="trent_dissents_from_the_definition_steps"></a>
**`trent_dissents_from_the_definition_steps`**

**The same checks, from Trent's side.** Trent objects three times to the
Reformed steps over its definition.

- Its reading of Paul's word objects to a starting point of the step about the
  word, not to the step.
- Its definition, taken as a claim about what God does, is stated and not argued
  against Paul's gospel.
- Its denial that faith suffices is an argument against Luke 18's step under the
  tradition standard only, because its one starting point is the definition.

So the support for the step about Paul's word stands at `wellSupported` under
all three standards: the strongest known objection to it is written down, and
fails.

```lean
theorem trent_dissents_from_the_definition_steps :
    trentWordOnLexicalAssessment.findings.kind = Findings.Kind.deniesGrounds ∧
    trentGraceOnGospelAssessment.findings.kind = Findings.Kind.asserted ∧
    trentSufficiencyOnLuke18Assessment.profile = [(Standard.evidence, false),
    (Standard.tradition, true), (Standard.scriptural, false)] ∧
    lexicalWordStep.ratings = [(Standard.evidence, Computed.stands
    Confidence.wellSupported), (Standard.tradition, Computed.stands
    Confidence.wellSupported), (Standard.scriptural, Computed.stands
    Confidence.wellSupported)]
-- axioms: propext
```

#### The debate heard under each standard

<a id="jamesRegister"></a>
**`jamesRegister`**

**The record for the debate over James.** Each position that objects to a step
of the Reformed reading is entered as an objection and assessed, together with
the two steps they are rated against. The other positions hold those steps, or
are readings of texts that the texts themselves answer.

```lean
def jamesRegister : Register jamesDispute :=
  {
    assessmentOf := fun x =>
      match x with
      | JamesParty.trentOnTheWord => some trentWordAssessment
      | JamesParty.trentOnWorks => some canon24Assessment
      | JamesParty.trentOnReward => some rewardAssessment
      | JamesParty.renewalOnTheWord => some renewalAssessment
      | JamesParty.westminsterOnReward =>
        some westminsterAssessment
      | x => none,
    ownPosition := jamesRegister._proof_1,
    steps :=
      [fruitStep, lexicalStep, canon24Step,
        rewardStep] }
```

<a id="ratedStrength"></a>
**`ratedStrength`**

Each position's weakest link under a given standard. It is as cited, with one
exception: under the tradition standard the argument from James's word is
weighed as `disputed`, which is what is worked out for it there.

```lean
def ratedStrength : Standard → JamesParty → ℕ :=
  fun x x_1 =>
    match x, x_1 with
    | Standard.tradition, JamesParty.lexical => 0
    | x, i => jamesPartyStrength i
```

<a id="rerated_strength"></a>
**`rerated_strength`**

Each position's weakest link, as worked out from its premises with the ratings
for that standard.

```lean
theorem rerated_strength : ∀ (s : Standard) (i : JamesParty),
    ((jamesRegister.rerated s).node i).strength = ratedStrength s i
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="ratedDefeats"></a>
**`ratedDefeats`**

Who defeats whom under a given standard. Under the evidence standard, as in the
full debate. Under the tradition standard there is one difference: Trent's
reading of the word and the reading through Paul each defeat the argument from
James's word, now that it is weighed as `disputed`.

```lean
def ratedDefeats : Standard → JamesParty → JamesParty → Prop :=
  fun x x_1 x_2 =>
    match x, x_1, x_2 with
    | Standard.tradition, JamesParty.trentOnTheWord,
      JamesParty.lexical => True
    | Standard.tradition, JamesParty.renewalOnTheWord,
      JamesParty.lexical => True
    | x, i, j => jamesPartyDefeats i j
```

<a id="instDecidableRelJamesPartyRatedDefeats"></a>
**`instDecidableRelJamesPartyRatedDefeats`**

The table is finite, so membership in it is decidable.

```lean
def instDecidableRelJamesPartyRatedDefeats : (s : Standard) → DecidableRel
    (ratedDefeats s)
```

<a id="rerated_defeats"></a>
**`rerated_defeats`**

**Who defeats whom under each standard.**

```lean
theorem rerated_defeats : ∀ (s : Standard) (i j : JamesParty),
    (jamesRegister.rerated s).defeats i j ↔ ratedDefeats s i j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="ratedFinite"></a>
**`ratedFinite`**

The debate under a given standard, in the form the solver works with.

```lean
def ratedFinite : (s : Standard) → Solver.Finite (jamesRegister.rerated
    s).defeats :=
  fun s =>
    { parties := jamesFinite.parties,
      complete := ratedFinite._proof_1,
      defeats := fun i j => decide (ratedDefeats s i j), spec := ⋯ }
```

<a id="jamesUnderEvidence"></a>
**`jamesUnderEvidence`**

The debate heard under the evidence standard.

```lean
def jamesUnderEvidence : Dispute Claim { i // jamesRegister.admits
    Standard.evidence i } :=
  jamesRegister.hearing Standard.evidence
```

<a id="jamesUnderTradition"></a>
**`jamesUnderTradition`**

The debate heard under the tradition standard.

```lean
def jamesUnderTradition : Dispute Claim { i // jamesRegister.admits
    Standard.tradition i } :=
  jamesRegister.hearing Standard.tradition
```

<a id="jamesUnderFinite"></a>
**`jamesUnderFinite`**

The debate heard under a standard, in the form the solver works with.

```lean
def jamesUnderFinite : (s : Standard) → Solver.Finite fun i j =>
    (jamesRegister.rerated s).defeats ↑i ↑j :=
  fun s => (ratedFinite s).restrict (jamesRegister.admits s)
```

<a id="jamesUnderEvidence_defeats"></a>
**`jamesUnderEvidence_defeats`**

**Who defeats whom under the evidence standard**: as in the full debate, among
the positions heard.

```lean
theorem jamesUnderEvidence_defeats : ∀ (i j : { i // jamesRegister.admits
    Standard.evidence i }), jamesUnderEvidence.defeats i j ↔ ratedDefeats
    Standard.evidence ↑i ↑j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="jamesUnderTradition_defeats"></a>
**`jamesUnderTradition_defeats`**

**Who defeats whom under the tradition standard**: the argument from James's
word, weighed as `disputed`, and the reading through Paul defeat each other.

```lean
theorem jamesUnderTradition_defeats : ∀ (i j : { i // jamesRegister.admits
    Standard.tradition i }), jamesUnderTradition.defeats i j ↔ ratedDefeats
    Standard.tradition ↑i ↑j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="underEvidenceSettled"></a>
**`underEvidenceSettled`**

How the debate is settled under the evidence standard. The argument from James's
word, the argument about James's faith, the Reformed reconciliation and the
Greek of both verses are accepted first, and nothing heard answers them. Trent's
Latin readings fall to the Greek. Every objection of Trent's to a rated step,
namely canon 24, chapter 16, the reading through Paul, and Trent's reading of
the word, either rests at some claim on the council's word or merely states its
denial, and so is not heard.

**What the dispute forces is exactly *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *Harmonisation of James 2:24*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*, *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*.**

- Stage 1: *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *Harmonisation of James 2:24*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*, *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*.
  - *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)* is defeated by nothing.
  - *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)* is defeated by nothing.
  - *Harmonisation of James 2:24* is defeated by nothing.
  - *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek* is defeated by nothing.
  - *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* is defeated by nothing.
  - *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)* is defeated by nothing.
- Nothing else is forced:
  - *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek* defeats *Revelation 22:11, as Trent quotes it*, and nothing forced defeats *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*.
  - *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* defeats *Sirach 18:22, as Trent quotes it*, and nothing forced defeats *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 2 defeats and 48 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`jamesUnderEvidence_defeats`](#jamesUnderEvidence_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - Outside Paul, ‘justify’ (δικαιόω) declares or vindicates; it does not mean making righteous — [Bauer 2000](../bibliography.md#bauer-danker-lexicon-2000), §s.v. δικαιόω; Deut 25:1; Matt 11:19; Luke 7:35; [The Holy Bible, English Standard Version 2001](../bibliography.md#crossway-esv-2001), ad loc. Matt 11:19
  - A word contributes the least meaning its context requires; one occurrence does not carry the whole concept — [Silva 1994](../bibliography.md#silva-biblical-words-1994); [Joos 1972](../bibliography.md#joos-semantic-axiom-1972); [Barr 2004](../bibliography.md#barr-semantics-2004)
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:21; [Silva 1994](../bibliography.md#silva-biblical-words-1994); [Barr 2004](../bibliography.md#barr-semantics-2004)
- *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - The faith alone that James 2:24 denies justifies is the dead faith of 2:14–26 — Jas 2:14-26; [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 7; [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24; [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XI.2
- *Harmonisation of James 2:24*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24; [Calvin 1960](../bibliography.md#calvin-institutes-1960), §III.xvii.11
- *Revelation 22:11, as Trent quotes it*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Revelation 22:11 says: he that is just, let him be justified still — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
- *Sirach 18:22, as Trent quotes it*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Sirach 18:22 says: be not afraid to be justified even to death — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
- *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - an inference step — [Pius XII 1943](../bibliography.md#pius-divino-afflante-spiritu-1943), §§16; [Holmes 2010](../bibliography.md#holmes-sblgnt-2010); [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011)
- *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - The Greek of Sirach 18:22 is about paying a vow: do not wait until death to be justified — [Swete](../bibliography.md#swete-old-testament-in-greek), ad loc. Sir 18:22; [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011), §Sirach 18:22
  - an inference step — [Pius XII 1943](../bibliography.md#pius-divino-afflante-spiritu-1943), §§16; [Holmes 2010](../bibliography.md#holmes-sblgnt-2010); [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011)
- *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XVI.5, XVI.6

<a id="underTraditionSettled"></a>
**`underTraditionSettled`**

How the debate is settled under the tradition standard. The argument about
James's faith and the Greek of both verses are accepted first. The argument from
James's word and the reading through Paul defeat each other. So do the Reformed
reconciliation and each of Trent's readings of what works do. Only Trent's
reading of the word is not heard.

**What the dispute forces is exactly *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*.**

- Stage 1: *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*.
  - *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)* is defeated by nothing.
  - *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek* is defeated by nothing.
  - *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* is defeated by nothing.
- Nothing else is forced:
  - *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)* defeats *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, and nothing forced defeats *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)*.
  - *James 2:24, read by canon 24* defeats *Harmonisation of James 2:24*, and nothing forced defeats *James 2:24, read by canon 24*.
  - *Harmonisation of James 2:24* defeats *James 2:24, read by canon 24*, and nothing forced defeats *Harmonisation of James 2:24*.
  - *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek* defeats *Revelation 22:11, as Trent quotes it*, and nothing forced defeats *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*.
  - *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* defeats *Sirach 18:22, as Trent quotes it*, and nothing forced defeats *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*.
  - *Harmonisation of James 2:24* defeats *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, and nothing forced defeats *Harmonisation of James 2:24*.
  - *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)* defeats *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)*, and nothing forced defeats *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*.
  - *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)* defeats *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*, and nothing forced defeats *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 8 defeats and 48 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`jamesUnderTradition_defeats`](#jamesUnderTradition_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, weakest at *disputed*:

Why the reading through Paul can be defended under the tradition standard: it
answers the argument from James's word, now that the two are rated alike.

***James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)* is accepted on some resolution.**

<a id="james_word_turns_on_the_standard"></a>
**`james_word_turns_on_the_standard`**

**What James's "justified" means depends on the standard, and the verdict and
the rating agree.**

Under the evidence standard the argument from James's word is forced, with the
argument about James's faith and the Greek of both verses. The reading through
Paul is not heard, because it rests on Trent's word that James's "justified"
(δικαιόω) is Paul's.

Under the tradition standard the reading through Paul is heard, the step about
the word is weighed at the rating worked out for it there, `disputed`, and
whether James's word means the increase of justice is contested. Each side can
be defended, and neither is forced.

```lean
theorem james_word_turns_on_the_standard : Framework.grounded
    jamesUnderEvidence.defeats = Solver.toSet (Witness.listSub
    (jamesRegister.admits Standard.evidence) [JamesParty.lexical,
    JamesParty.faith, JamesParty.harmony, JamesParty.revelationText,
    JamesParty.sirachText, JamesParty.westminsterOnReward]) ∧ Nonempty
    (Contested jamesUnderTradition (p Claim.jamesJustifyDenotesIncrease))
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="under_tradition_forces"></a>
**`under_tradition_forces`**

**Under the tradition standard, what is forced is the argument about James's
faith and the Greek of the two verses**, and no more.

```lean
theorem under_tradition_forces : Framework.grounded
    jamesUnderTradition.defeats = Solver.toSet (Witness.listSub
    (jamesRegister.admits Standard.tradition) [JamesParty.faith,
    JamesParty.revelationText, JamesParty.sirachText])
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="trentOnReward_denies_fruit"></a>
**`trentOnReward_denies_fruit`**

Trent's reading of the reward texts denies that works are fruit and not ground.

```lean
theorem trentOnReward_denies_fruit : Entails (jamesDispute.node
    JamesParty.trentOnReward).premises (∼p Claim.worksAreFruitNotGround)
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

- *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Paul's word ‘justify’ means the renewal of the inward man, not only a verdict — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, chs. 7–8; [VanLandingham 2006](../bibliography.md#vanlandingham-judgment-justification-2006)
  - James's ‘justify’ (δικαιόω) has the sense Paul's has: the justification of Romans and Galatians — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10; [VanLandingham 2006](../bibliography.md#vanlandingham-judgment-justification-2006)
- *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XVI.5, XVI.6

<a id="rewardHeard"></a>
**`rewardHeard`**

Why chapter 16's reading of the reward texts can be defended there: it answers
the Reformed reconciliation.

***The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *James 2:24, read by canon 24*, *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* can be held.
- None of *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, *James 2:24, read by canon 24*, *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:
  - *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)* defeats *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, and *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)* defeats *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)*.
  - *Harmonisation of James 2:24* defeats *James 2:24, read by canon 24*, and *James 2:24, read by canon 24* defeats *Harmonisation of James 2:24*.
  - *Harmonisation of James 2:24* defeats *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, and *James 2:24, read by canon 24* defeats *Harmonisation of James 2:24*.
  - *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)* defeats *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, and *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)* defeats *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 7 defeats and 62 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`jamesUnderTradition_defeats`](#jamesUnderTradition_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *James's word (δικαιόω, by the rule of least meaning)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:21; [Silva 1994](../bibliography.md#silva-biblical-words-1994); [Barr 2004](../bibliography.md#barr-semantics-2004)
- *James's faith (the faith James calls dead)*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - The faith alone that James 2:24 denies justifies is the dead faith of 2:14–26 — Jas 2:14-26; [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 7; [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24; [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XI.2
- *James 2:24, read by canon 24*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Good works are a cause of the increase of justification, not merely its fruits — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), canon 24
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), canon 24
- *The reward of works (Trent, Session VI, ch. 16)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - The reward God renders to the works of the justified is rendered to them as merits — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 16; canon 32; [Dulles 1999](../bibliography.md#dulles-two-languages-1999)
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 16, canon 32; [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XVI.5, XVI.6
- *Revelation 22:11, in the Greek*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - an inference step — [Pius XII 1943](../bibliography.md#pius-divino-afflante-spiritu-1943), §§16; [Holmes 2010](../bibliography.md#holmes-sblgnt-2010); [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011)
- *Sirach 18:22, in the Greek*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - The Greek of Sirach 18:22 is about paying a vow: do not wait until death to be justified — [Swete](../bibliography.md#swete-old-testament-in-greek), ad loc. Sir 18:22; [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011), §Sirach 18:22
  - an inference step — [Pius XII 1943](../bibliography.md#pius-divino-afflante-spiritu-1943), §§16; [Holmes 2010](../bibliography.md#holmes-sblgnt-2010); [United States Conference of Catholic Bishops 2011](../bibliography.md#usccb-nabre-2011)
- *Harmonisation of James 2:24*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XVI.2, XVI.5; [Lutheran World Federation and Catholic Church 2000](../bibliography.md#lwf-catholic-joint-declaration-2000), §§§25, 37; see §38
  - an inference step — [Moo 2000](../bibliography.md#moo-james-2000), ad loc. Jas 2:24; [Calvin 1960](../bibliography.md#calvin-institutes-1960), §III.xvii.11
- *Revelation 22:11, as Trent quotes it*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Revelation 22:11 says: he that is just, let him be justified still — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
- *Sirach 18:22, as Trent quotes it*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Sirach 18:22 says: be not afraid to be justified even to death — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
- *James's word, read through Paul's (the renewal reading)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - Paul's word ‘justify’ means the renewal of the inward man, not only a verdict — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), Decree on Justification, chs. 7–8; [VanLandingham 2006](../bibliography.md#vanlandingham-judgment-justification-2006)
  - James's ‘justify’ (δικαιόω) has the sense Paul's has: the justification of Romans and Galatians — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 10; [VanLandingham 2006](../bibliography.md#vanlandingham-judgment-justification-2006)
- *The reward of works, of grace (Westminster XVI.5, XVI.6)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - an inference step — [Westminster Assembly 1647](../bibliography.md#westminster-confession-1647), §XVI.5, XVI.6

<a id="fruit_turns_on_the_standard"></a>
**`fruit_turns_on_the_standard`**

**Whether works are fruit and not ground depends on whether a council's word
counts, and the verdict and the rating agree.**

Under the evidence standard the Reformed reconciliation is forced. It derives
"fruit, not ground" from Westminster's proof texts. Neither of Trent's
objections is heard: each rests at one claim on the council's word.

Under the tradition standard both are heard, the step is weighed at `disputed`,
and the question is contested. The reconciliation and chapter 16's reading of
the reward texts can each be defended, and neither is forced.

```lean
theorem fruit_turns_on_the_standard : Framework.grounded
    jamesUnderEvidence.defeats = Solver.toSet (Witness.listSub
    (jamesRegister.admits Standard.evidence) [JamesParty.lexical,
    JamesParty.faith, JamesParty.harmony, JamesParty.revelationText,
    JamesParty.sirachText, JamesParty.westminsterOnReward]) ∧ Nonempty
    (Contested jamesUnderTradition (p Claim.worksAreFruitNotGround))
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```
